clue.text: One would not wish one's kids to be brought up in it

definitions.text: One would not wish one's kids to be brought up in it

parts.words: One would not wish one's kids to be brought up in it
parts.note: reads like a remark about a bad neighbourhood for raising children, but 'brought up' also means made to appear before magistrates, and the place meant is where young offenders are tried

explanation.surface: A parent's worry about the wrong place to raise a family.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth tribunal is where young offenders are 'brought up', that is charged and tried, which no parent wants for their children.

clue.text: Hardy hero-subject due for a change

indicators.note: asks for the letters of the words before it to be changed round into a new order

explanation.surface: A Hardy protagonist whose subject is overdue for some variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy hero' looks like the definition, but 'hero' is part of the fodder; 'Hardy' alone defines, standing for a novel by Thomas Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's last novel, so it is 'a Hardy' in the way one speaks of owning a Dickens.

clue.text: Arrived from France for Twickenham, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the French past participle of venir, to come, in its feminine form means 'arrived'
Twickenham is the London stadium that is the home of English rugby union, an example of a place where events are held

explanation.surface: A French arrival bound for the home of English rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'come' or 'arrived', and in English a sports ground or meeting place such as Twickenham stadium.

clue.text: Incorrigible oilfield: idler?

definitions.meaning: describing someone hopeless who never mends their ways
a whimsical reading: a bore in an oilfield that never produces anything would be a well that never does

explanation.surface: An oilfield that is hopelessly lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiftless good-for-nothing is beyond reform; read literally, 'never do well' suits an unproductive oil bore.

clue.text: Old rate of exchange is tight on one

indicators.note: exchange means swapping things round, so the letters of the two words before are swapped into a new order

explanation.surface: An old currency exchange rate that pinches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate of exchange' reads as a financial phrase, but 'of exchange' is the anagram signal working on OLDRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer's or gymnast's close-fitting one-piece garment clings to the body of whoever wears it.

clue.text: Price a Broadway production for the Big Apple

parts.note: the price of something is its cost
a broad way is a road, abbreviated RD

explanation.surface: Costing a Broadway show for New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Apple' wants to be New York; it is literally a large apple. 'production' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large old English variety of cooking apple, hence a big apple.

clue.text: Single piece of ammunition

indicators.note: only a piece of the word ammunition is taken, the letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: One single round of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is one single thing, a whole counted as one.

clue.text: One of those known to expert arboriculturists..?

definitions.text: One of those known to expert arboriculturists..?

parts.words: One of those known to expert arboriculturists..?
parts.note: the plant's name sounds, loosely, like 'tree-knowing', which is what a tree expert does, while it is really a bulb-bearing plant

explanation.surface: A plant that only specialist tree growers would recognise.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to the next clue, which plays the same tree game.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of allium that bears little bulbs at the top of its stalk, so a gardener's plant with a tree-like name.

clue.text: … House-sage?

parts.note: continues the tree theme: a wise old figure in the House of parliament, whose title begins with the name of a tree

explanation.surface: A wise figure of the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran politician respected for experience, a wise old head in Parliament.

clue.text: Priestley's corner exposed

definitions.meaning: J. B. Priestley wrote the 1932 play '... Corner'
exposed to harm, risky or perilous

explanation.surface: Priestley's corner is left open to view.
explanation.definitionFit: Completes the title of J. B. Priestley's play, and also means risky or unsafe.

clue.text: Euclid's fifth proposition, perfect in conception

indicators.note: the fifth letter of the word Euclid is picked

parts.note: a proposition is an offer or deal

explanation.surface: A geometry theorem by Euclid, perfect as conceived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Euclid's fifth proposition' reads as a theorem in geometry, but 'fifth' picks the letter I and 'proposition' is a business offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect as imagined, existing as a concept in the mind.

clue.text: Harris, for example, in river

definitions.meaning: Harris is a famous handwoven woollen cloth from the Scottish Outer Hebrides
a river forming part of the border between Scotland and England

explanation.surface: Someone called Harris swimming in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough woollen fabric of which Harris cloth is a type, and the Scottish border river.

clue.text: Whaler's cry of surprise touches sailor

indicators.note: one piece touches the next, so the two are placed side by side

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of surprise
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A whaling man's exclamation of surprise reaches a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain of the Pequod in Melville's Moby-Dick, the most famous whaling captain in fiction.

clue.text: Hand-out of old-fashioned quarter

definitions.meaning: a charitable distribution, or state unemployment benefit
an archaic word for a portion or share dealt out

explanation.surface: Charity handed out in an old part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit payment or charitable gift, and in old usage a person's allotted share or portion.

clue.text: Have a flutter, if it be all right, playing roulette

indicators.note: roulette is a game of chance, so the letters land in a random new order

explanation.surface: A gambler deciding to bet at the roulette wheel if all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a flutter' suggests a small bet, which suits the surface; here it means the heart quivering. The anagram takes IFITBEALL plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibrillation is rapid irregular twitching of heart muscle, a medical flutter.

clue.text: Purpose to marry, clutching ring? That's settled!

indicators.note: the two joined words hold the next piece in their grasp, around it

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
to wed is to marry
the letter O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone intent on marriage grabs a ring, and the matter is decided.
explanation.definitionFit: Property is endowed on someone when it is formally settled on them, as in a marriage settlement.

clue.text: Losing points at end of season, like Forest perhaps

definitions.text: Losing points at end of season, like Forest perhaps

parts.words: Losing points at end of season, like Forest perhaps
parts.note: reads as Nottingham Forest football club dropping points late in the season, but it means trees in a forest shedding their pointed leaves in autumn

explanation.surface: A football team such as Nottingham Forest slumps late in the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club; the 'points' are really leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees that shed their foliage each autumn, as most woodland does.

clue.text: Chars papers

definitions.meaning: a char is a British word for a cleaning woman, also called a daily
newspapers published every day

explanation.surface: Burns some newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for cleaners who come in each day, and for newspapers issued every day.

clue.text: Bellyache after half the buns in the country?

indicators.note: the stomach-ache piece comes after the other in the answer
takes the first half of the word that follows

parts.note: colic is a severe bellyache

explanation.surface: A stomach-ache after eating half the buns, out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic and pastoral, relating to rural life.

clue.text: Joy at No 10 for so long?

parts.note: cheer is gladness or joy
the number 10, as printed, looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Celebration at Downing Street as a Prime Minister departs.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence; the digits 1 and 0 are read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual British farewell, the same as saying goodbye.

clue.text: In rivers I am pitiless: I rip a nasty hole away, initially

indicators.note: the opening letter of each word in the run is taken

explanation.surface: A ferocious river fish boasting of tearing holes in its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American freshwater fish famed for its ferocity and razor teeth.

clue.text: Gemstone looks awful mounted in earthenware vessel

indicators.note: the turned word is put inside the vessel

parts.note: a pot is an earthenware vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means going upwards, so the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: dire means awful

explanation.surface: A gem set in a clay pot looks terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks' is a link word; 'mounted' turns DIRE into ERID, which goes inside POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A green semi-precious stone, a gem variety of olivine.

clue.text: Secret signals from the canon

definitions.meaning: a system of disguised messages
a canon is a body of rules or laws, a set of principles

explanation.surface: Coded messages sent from the cathedral clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher for secret messages, and a systematic body of laws.

clue.text: Bring up buck

definitions.meaning: to raise children
a horse bucks or rises on its hind legs

explanation.surface: Raise a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise children, and for a horse to rise up on its hind legs.

clue.text: Liberal church recess is a mistake

parts.note: an apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: Liberal-minded church alcove is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or error, a temporary failure of concentration.

clue.text: Coming before a superior

definitions.meaning: earlier in time or order
the head of a religious house, ranking just below an abbot

explanation.surface: Approaching a senior person.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier or previous, and a monk in charge of a priory.

clue.text: Pure water

definitions.meaning: sheer, nothing more than
a lake or pond

explanation.surface: Clean water.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothing more than, sheer; and a small lake.

clue.text: Flower for right-handed person?

parts.note: RH is the abbreviation for right-handed
one stands for a person, as in 'one can try'

explanation.surface: A bloom picked for someone who uses their right hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword convention for a river, something that flows; here the river through France.
explanation.definitionFit: A great French river, a 'flow-er' in crossword terms.

clue.text: Set terms paid for obstruction in business

indicators.note: the letters are set out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fixed fees paid to clear a business blockage.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive bureaucratic formality that holds up official or commercial dealings.

clue.text: Consult rail timetable and watch departures of those detailed?

definitions.meaning: check the times of trains
the nursery rhyme's three blind mice had their tails cut off, so they are 'de-tailed', and the rhyme's line tells us to observe them running off

explanation.surface: Checking the train timetable and seeing off the passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally checking train times, and a line from the rhyme about three blind mice whose tails were cut off.
